assumptions.income_quintile: personal labour + business income quintile among two-year earners, followed in employed years; independent of the household income band (v1)
assumptions.forward_kernels: 2024 income transitions re-fitted to 2024 margins on the baseline (frozen for scenarios), 2025 employment level (panel), 2025 migration flows, 2025 marriage/divorce rates, 2024 life table

employment.note: Personas work more often than the survey (2025 level = panel); the change over years follows the published rates, so the panel - official gap should stay roughly constant.

income.model: Markov on published 5x5 transitions by year x sex x prior-year age, mover-stayer mix, transitions re-fitted each year to the published margins; stayers lapse at 65

income_amount.model: nominal annual labour + business income: sex x age-band lognormal from the published wage-job mean/median of the year, truncated to the national band of the person's quintile; within-band rank AR(1) rho=0.6; levels beyond the last table extrapolate each cell's 5-year compound growth

smoking.note: district_rate_mean is the unweighted mean of the panel members' district rates (조율), which the panel tracks by construction; it is not the national rate.

residence.note: Panel is 19+, the official yearly share is of all ages (movers / ~51.7M). Mobility propensity (Gamma, mean 1, shape k) is sized on the 2005 census five-year question, the latest published by age; today's moves are rarer, so the panel five-year shares should sit somewhat below 2005.

forward.scenario: each year 5 more in 100 of the bottom quintile move up one quintile (an assumed policy effect, not an estimate); same random numbers as the baseline
